newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says Bre-X gold licence not cleared yet.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says Bre-X gold licence not cleared yet.

text.p: Indonesia's Director General of Mining Kuntoro Mangkusubroto said on Thursday the government is still witholding contracts of work related to the Busang gold find controlled by Bre-X Minerals Ltd of Canada.
"Two applications from Bre-X...cannot be processed because there is a dispute with its Indonesian partner," Kuntoro said in a statement made available to Reuters.
Indonesian businessman Jusuf Merukh has said he has a 20 percent claim on Busang and an option for an additional 20 percent. Bre-X has contested his claims.

The Indonesian government has so far refused to grant Bre-X contracts of work needed to further explore and develop the two richest sections of the property and said it will not do so until the dispute is resolved.
"The government is still giving a chance to parties in the dispute to solve their problem before their applications are processed further," Kuntoro said.
The Busang gold fields are in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province on Borneo island and are estimated to contain at least 47 million ounces of gold.

On Monday, Bre-X announced a deal with a company controlled by President Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto for consultation and other services in relation to the Busang field under which it is to receive a 10-percent interest in the richest parts of the find and a fee of $40 million over four months.
The deal is subject to Bre-X being granted the contracts of work.
